summary: Implementation of the APTEL judgment dated 17.7.2025 in Appeal No. 92/2017 (NLCIL vs CERC & ors.) The tariff for NLC TPS-II, Stage-I (3x210 MW) & Stage-II (4x210 MW) for the period from 1.4.2009 to 31.3.2014 was determined by the Commission vide its order dated 27.6.2011 in Petition No. 231/2009, in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2009 (in short, “2009 Tariff Regulations”). Aggrieved by certain findings in the said order, the Petitioner, Neyveli Lignite Corporation Limited (in short ‘NLCIL’) filed Review Petition No. 17/RP/2011 seeking review on specific issues. The Commission disposed of the said Review Petition vide order dated Tariff Regulations. The Commission, vide order dated 10.2.2017 in Petition No. 473/GT/2014, revised the tariff of NLC TPS-II Stage I & II after the truing-up exercise. 2. Aggrieved by the said order dated 10.2.2017, the NLCIL filed Appeal No. 92 of 2017 4. Accordingly, APTEL, vide judgment dated 17.7.2025, remanded the matter to the Commission for reconsideration and directed as under: 5. Pursuant to the judgment dated 17.7.2025 of APTEL, the Petition was taken up for hearing on 23.9.2025. The Commission, vide the ROP (record of proceedings) of the hearing dated 23.9.2025, directed NLCIL to furnish additional information. NLCIL, vide an affidavit dated 14.10.2025, submitted the information in compliance with the Commission’s directions . The matter was thereafter heard on 18.11.2025 and on 2.1.2026. The Commission, after hearing the parties on 2.1.2026, reserved the order after permitting the parties to file their written note of submissions. NLCIL has placed its written submission on record. 6. Based on the submissions of the parties and the material available on record, we now proceed to examine the remand directions issued by APTEL and issues raised by NLCIL in respect of the issues (a), (b) and (c), as mentioned in para 4 above. - order, but not to entertain a collateral attempt by TANGEDCO to re litigate the same legal objections that were rejected by APTEL. _(b) The petitioner seeks permission of the Commission for substitution of the actual SFC in lieu of normative SFC, hitherto applied by NLC in the ECR determination under Regulation 21(6) for the period 2009-14, in accordance with the Para12 of the order in Petition No. 285/MP/2013 and to recover from the beneficiaries along with interest, the differential amount due to revision of ECR consequent to application of actual SFC in lieu of Normative SFC in the algorithm.”_ 13. The Commission, vide order dated 10.2.2017 in Petition No. 473/GT/2014, disposed of the contention of NLCIL for substitution of actual SFC in lieu of normative SFC with the _“73. The petitioner in this petition has also sought for substitution of the actual SFC in lieu of normative SFC, in the ECR determination under Regulation 21(6) for the period 2009-14, in terms of the order dated 10.7.2015. The Commission in its order dated 10.7.2015 while holding that the methodology adopted by NTPC was not in conformity to the Regulation 26(a) of the 2009 Tariff Regulations had observed that NTPC was charging less by applying the said methodology. Accordingly, the decision in the case of NTPC cannot be made applicable to the instant case of the petitioner. The petitioner has also prayed for recovery from the beneficiaries along with interest, the differential amount due to revision of ECR consequent to application of actual SFC in lieu of normative SFC. It is noticed that the Commission in the said order had clarified that the said decision cannot be used to reopen settled cases. In the light of the above discussions, the submissions of the petitioner are not acceptable and the prayer of the petitioner for substitution of the actual SFC in lieu of normative SFC in the ECR determination is accordingly rejected.”_ reasoning in its Order dated 10.7.2015 in Petition No. 285/MP/2013, to the effect that the decision in the case pertaining to NTPC Limited could not be applied to reopen settled cases, was incorrect. APTEL also clarified that once a particular methodology or formula has been accepted as valid in one case, the same should be applied uniformly in similar cases. Accordingly, APTEL set aside the Commission’s decision rejecting NLCIL’s claim for adjustment of Energy Charges based on actual SFC and directed the Commission to recalculate ECR in accordance with the methodology recognised in its earlier judgment dated 28.5.2020 in Appeal Nos. 291 and 344 of 2016. (v) The contention of TANGEDCO that Life Extension expenditure should not be recognised as assets is based on an incorrect interpretation of the regulatory provisions. Regulation 10 of the 2009 Tariff Regulations only bars revision of capital 39.
